fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. Verse 7 says the Israelites were fruitful, increased rapidly and became exceedingly numerous, “…so that the land was filled with them.” Verse 5 counts seventy descendants of Jacob, and now the land is packed. That's a family reunion that got WAY out of hand.

Jacob's family did come into Egypt from Canaan (Genesis 46:6). But nothing in this passage has them heading back. Verse 7 says the land was filled with them, so they stay and keep growing. I don't see a moving truck anywhere in this chapter.

That's right, baker. In verse 9 the king tells his people, “the Israelites have become too numerous and too powerful for us.” Then he says, “Come, let us deal shrewdly with them, or they will increase even more…” I think a growing crowd has him rattled. That's the whole plan, and it's not a kind one.

Those two names do show up together, friend. Genesis 10:11 lists Nineveh and Calah in the same list, with Rehoboth-Ir between them. But the store cities the Israelites built for Pharaoh in Exodus 1:11 are Pithom and Rameses.

That's the one. Verse 12 says the Egyptians came to dread the Israelites. The Israelites keep multiplying and flourishing, and the Egyptians dread them. I think the king's plan landed him somewhere he didn't plan to be.

That would be a softer ending, friend, but it's not what the text says. In verse 12 the Egyptians came to dread the Israelites. And verses 13-14 say they worked the Israelites ruthlessly, and every service they imposed was harsh.

I can see why you'd think it, since the king is the one giving orders. But verse 17 says the midwives “…did not do as the king of Egypt had instructed; they let the boys live.” Shiphrah and Puah were told one thing and did another.

That's it, friend. Verse 17 says the midwives feared God and did not do as the king had instructed. The text gives that as the reason. The king gave the order, and fear of God is what the text says stood behind what they did.

You've got it. Verse 21 says, “And because the midwives feared God, He gave them families of their own.” The text gives their fear of God as the reason. And the gift is a personal one: families of their own.
